items.stimulus: An immunology lab counts white blood cells using a slide etched with square grids. On one slide, square $A$ is a small counting square. Square $B$ is a larger counting square whose side length is $3$ times the side length of square $A$.
items.stem: The area of square $B$ is $k$ times the area of square $A$. What is the value of $k$?
items.explanation: The scale factor for lengths is $k = 3$. Areas scale by the square of the length factor, so square $B$'s area is $3^2 = 9$ times square $A$'s area. To check, give square $A$ a side of $1$: its area is $1$, and square $B$ has side $3$ and area $9$.

A.why: You gave the ratio of the side lengths, $3$, as the ratio of the areas. Areas scale by $k^2$, not by $k$.

B.why: You doubled the scale factor ($2 \times 3$) when you needed to square it ($3 \times 3$).

D.why: You cubed the scale factor, which gives the ratio of volumes. A square is flat, so its area scales by $3^2$, not $3^3$.
